prose: Christian Kästner, who teaches the Machine Learning in Production course, describes what changed once AI agents could do all of his assignments. Back in 2021 GPT-3 was already passing his reading quizzes without seeing the assigned paper and he changed nothing; five years later he has redesigned most assessments around one strategy: no longer test understanding with anything done at home - evaluate through interactions with a TA, on exams, and on a video demo. The learning goals barely moved: engineering tradeoffs, anticipating and mitigating risks, teamwork - skills he thinks are still worth acquiring even if they can be simulated.

The uncomfortable part, he says upfront, is that AI is actively undermining evidence-based teaching practices. Frequent low-stakes assessment with feedback loses to exams when AI does the low-stakes work. His resubmission safety net - a core grading-for-equity recommendation - was being gamed: students submitted generated solutions unread, then used the grading feedback to resubmit, so resubmissions now carry a 10% penalty. In-class discussion questions get offloaded to models too, but pen-and-paper fixes would raise stress and delay feedback, so he errs toward keeping low-stakes interactions even when abusable. Students may use AI anywhere, in any form, without attribution, except in written and oral exams - policing is infeasible, and students need to learn responsible use anyway.
highlights: Kästner: GPT-3 was passing his reading quizzes in 2021; by 2026 agents do all assignments
New assessment strategy: nothing at-home tests understanding - TA interactions, exams, video demos
Learning goals unchanged: engineering tradeoffs, risk anticipation, teamwork
AI is undermining evidence-based pedagogy, he warns - low-stakes practice loses to exams
Resubmission safety net was gamed with generated-first drafts; now a 10% resubmission penalty
Students offload even in-class discussion questions to models
Policy: AI allowed everywhere, no attribution, except written and oral exams
His balance: accept some abuse to preserve a better environment for students who want to learn
